subject: binharic-cli
title: The real agent loop is a 400-line recursive function inside the zustand UI store, with tool gating, retry, interruption flags, and metrics all fused into store actions
one_why: Nuance on god-file-loop: not a big loop file but a loop with no headless seam at all - the store IS the harness, so nothing (tests, RPC, scripts) can drive the agent without the TUI.

subject: binharic-cli
title: PermissionsManager with rules, allow/block lists, session/project/global scopes and sensitive-path patterns has zero call sites in src or tests; the only permission logic that binds is a hardcoded read-only Set
evidence: src/agent/core/permissionsManager.ts:47,90,120; grep checkCommand/checkPath/PermissionsManager across src and tests: zero hits; real gate is state.ts:18-30,825
one_why: The file reads like the project has a configurable policy engine; it does not - a reviewer or user trusting the surface gets a fixed allowlist and a prompt.

subject: binharic-cli
title: Risk-tiered checkpoint system (handler registry + deny-on-critical default + UI dialog) is never registered or invoked: pendingCheckpoint is rendered by App but nothing ever sets it
evidence: src/agent/core/checkpoints.ts:20,30,43-47 (requestCheckpoint denies critical without handler), :58 (assessRiskLevel); src/ui/App.tsx:90 + CheckpointConfirmation.tsx:24; grep setCheckpointHandler/requestCheckpoint in src outside checkpoints.ts: zero hits
one_why: Same concept as -2 but separate machinery; together they mean two independent safety UIs/policies exist purely as scenery next to one working approval gate.

subject: binharic-cli
title: 37 of 88 test files never import anything from src: they reimplement the logic under test inline (timeouts, loops) or assert tautologies, inflating test_loc and the green badge without testing production code
evidence: grep: 51/88 test files import src; tests/agent/bugs/streamTimeoutBug.test.ts:19-45 (rebuilds timeout harness locally); tests/agent/tools/safeToolAutoExecution.test.ts:59 (expect(toolName).toBeTruthy()); tests/agent/core/codeQualityFixes.test.ts:174,178,200 (toBeDefined existence checks)
one_why: Distinct from faux-provider-testing (that mocks the model, still drives real code) and from fixture LOC inflation: here the code under test is the test, so regressions in state.ts pass CI; coverage badge masks that the real approval gate has zero coverage.

subject: binharic-cli
title: bash tool guards spawn of /bin/bash with four regexes (rm -rf /, mkfs, dd if=, fork bomb) that a one-line rewording or nested shell bypasses
one_why: Mitigated but not fixed by default approval (bash not in SAFE_AUTO_TOOLS, state.ts:825): the denylist adds theater and could lull an approver who assumes blocked==safe.

subject: binharic-cli
title: A second, 'advanced' agent layer (AI SDK Experimental_Agent x6, budget/error/validation stop conditions, phase-based tool selector, context manager, tool-result summarizer) is unreachable from the product - only tests construct it, so CI exercises a loop users never run
evidence: src/agent/core/agents.ts:33-62,108,144,177,210; src/agent/execution/loopControl.ts; src/agent/execution/prepareStep.ts:32-51,106; grep createBinharicAgent/createAgentByType in src outside agents.ts: zero hits (test files only)
one_why: Worst-case pairing with replica-tests: agents.test.ts, safeToolAutoExecution.test.ts etc. prove behavior of code that never ships while the shipped state.ts loop stays untested; README/ROADMAP features trace to this dead layer.

subject: binharic-cli
title: When an edit's search string fails to match, a side-model call repairs it under a verbatim-presence constraint before retrying; malformed edit JSON gets a separate schema-constrained repair call
evidence: src/agent/tools/definitions/edit.ts:89; src/agent/workflows/autofix.ts:46-80 (fixEditPrompt + :65 'MUST be present verbatim in the file content'), :22-43 (autofixJson)
one_why: Cheap edit-failure recovery that keeps the loop moving without model-visible retry churn; the verbatim-in-file validation constraint is the part worth copying - the hardcoded gpt-5-mini fixer (autofix.ts:11) is not.

subject: binharic-cli
title: Real-path context management is drop-oldest-message trimming past 80% of context, with a token count that switches to a 0.4-tokens-per-char heuristic above 12k chars; the only summarizing compaction lives in the dead agent layer
evidence: src/agent/context/contextWindow.ts:7 (length*0.4), :63-101 (while-loop splice from index 1); dead summarizer: src/agent/execution/prepareStep.ts:106-120; second silent trim provider.ts:225-227 (history.maxItems slice)
one_why: Baseline rung below the 6-anchor 'one standard auto-summarize': trimming mid-conversation silently discards tool results the model references later, and the 0.4x heuristic miscounts exactly the large tool outputs that trigger trimming.

subject: binharic-cli
title: Stream-timeout watchdog throws inside a setTimeout callback, so the TransientError escapes the enclosing try and lands in the process-level uncaughtException handler instead of the intended retry path
evidence: src/agent/core/state.ts:676-687 (resetStreamTimeout -> throw new TransientError in timer body); outer catch at :913; process handler src/cli.ts:29-35
one_why: The advertised 2-minute stream-timeout retry (and its replica test streamTimeoutBug.test.ts) never fires in production; a stalled stream hangs the UI until the global handler logs it - and the test that 'covers' this is itself a replica (see -4).
